hazard_chain: 1. Massive wedge failure of ~27 million m³ rock and hanging glacier from Ronti peak (~5,600m ASL)
2. High-energy vertical free-fall of 1,800m pulverizing ice into frictional water/slurry
3. Hyper-velocity debris flow travelling down Ronti Gad and Rishiganga valley (>20 m/s)
4. Total destruction of Rishiganga 13.2 MW Small Hydro Project within 6 minutes
5. Impact on Tapovan Vishnugad 520 MW Hydro Project barrage and headrace tunnels
cause_primary: Catastrophic Rock-Ice Avalanche Detachment (No Rainfall Trigger)
cause_contributing: Permafrost warming and debuttressing of steep rock face
High structural kinetic energy melting embedded glacier ice instantaneously
Winter conditions without rainfall alert baseline — pure geomechanical/cryospheric trigger
data_availability_before_event: Seismic stations recorded precursory tremor at ~04:51 UTC, Sentinel-2 / Planet imagery showed wedge cracks in 2016-2020.

key_facts.fact: Over 200 fatalities and missing workers primarily at Tapovan tunnel and Rishiganga sites
Zero rainfall reported — weather was clear and sunny across Chamoli district on 7 Feb 2021
Flow peak discharge estimated at ~15,000 m³/s near Rishiganga confluence
key_facts.source: Nature Geoscience Multi-Author Consortium Study (Shugar et al., 2021)

evidence_claims.claim: 204 missing individuals across Tapovan, Raini, and downstream riverbeds.

lessons: Rainfall-only alert systems fail on cryospheric and mass-wasting triggers
Downstream hydro barrages require automated upstream radar/acoustic tripwires
Seismic signal inversion can provide a 10-15 minute early detection window

fingerprint.geology_type: Vaikrita Group High-Grade Metamorphic Gneiss & Hanging Ice
